title: Closing and Funding Interest Rate on a Prepaid Interest Dispute Excess
content:
**Standard.** In a Closing and Funding prepaid interest dispute decision, the interest rate on the excess is set as follows: where the closing record's loan amount differs from the loan file's loan amount or its note rate differs from the rate the lock holds, it is the rate the lock holds; where there is no such difference and the decision comes later than the dispute response business days (30) after the filing date, it is 2.0 percent; otherwise there is no interest.

Business days for these deadlines are counted Monday through Friday starting with the day after the filing date, and the decision date is the day the decision is booked. The records compared are the closing record, the borrower's Mortgage Loan File (its loan amount) and the borrower's Rate Lock Commitment (the rate the lock holds).

| Closing record differs from the file's loan amount or the lock's rate? | Decided later than 30 business days after filing? | Rate |
|---|---|---|
| Yes | either | the rate the lock holds |
| No | Yes | 2.0 percent |
| No | No | none |

## Interest on the excess

The interest on the excess is the excess times the interest rate taken as a percent, times the interest days, divided by the per diem day-count basis (365 under every closing method), rounded half up to the cent, and the refund is the excess plus that interest.

Hypothetical: an excess of 29.90 at 2.0 percent over 47 interest days gives 29.90 times 2.0 percent, times 47, divided by 365, which is 0.08 after rounding; the refund is 29.98.

## The 30-business-day line (hypothetical: filed on Monday 2 June)

Business day 1 is Tuesday 3 June and business day 30 is Monday 14 July. A decision on 14 July is not later than the line; a decision on 15 July is.
